messages:
Aisha: quick sync — we need to pick a calibration procedure for the FP8/INT8 rollout. two main axes: per-channel vs per-tensor, and outlier handling. also: kernel selection seems to flip based on calib stats and that impacts runtime (batching/KV behavior). thoughts? :thinking_face:
Ben: short version from my last run: per-channel reduced logprob regressions but caused runtime to pick a slower per-block INT8 kernel on a few layers. throughput dropped ~9% on 1k token sessions.
Carlos: ouch. do you have numbers? was KV warmup included?
Ben: included 1280-token contexts. profile snippet: 
```
[profile] model=rw-13b mode=per-channel samples=1024 trim=99.9
tried_kernels: int8_fast, int8_block, fp8_mixed
selected: int8_block (fallback from int8_fast due to overflow stats)
throughput: int8_fast=460 tok/s (fail), int8_block=420 tok/s, fp8_mixed=440 tok/s
```
Ben: so quality->per-channel helped, but scale ranges triggered int8_block which is slower on our runtime due to lack of fused ops for that layout.
Maria: fwiw I think a lot of the int8 failures are outlier-driven. when we include very long tails (huge sparse attention spikes) calibration scales explode. my two cents: percentile trimming is safer than max-abs. e.g. trim top 0.5% or 0.1%.
Carlos: agreed. also we should stratify samples by sequence length and domain. calibration set skewed to short prompts will misrepresent KV cache steady-state. we should mimic production batch sizes & seq distribution.
Aisha: proposal: two-pass calibrate pipeline. 1) quick per-tensor pass on stratified small sample (pick baseline kernels and params). 2) sensitivity scan: run flagged layers with per-channel quant (only where sensitivity>threshold) on a longer seq/cold->hot KV run. outlier handling: percentile trim 99.5, then clamp to 3 sigma for remaining extremes.
Maria: that seems reasonable. also add a KV-warmup run: run a few sequences that exercise prefix caching to capture activation stats that only appear once KV is warmed. otherwise kernel selection will ignore cache behavior.
Carlos: can we get a config snippet so I can run the experiment farm?
Aisha: yes, use this: 
``` 
# tools/calibrate.yaml
model: rw-13b
passes:
  - name: quick_tens
    mode: per-tensor
    samples: 512
    stratify: [short,mid,long]
    trim_pct: 99.5
  - name: sensitivity
    mode: per-channel
    samples: 256
    layers_to_probe: top_30_by_variance
    kv_warmup: true
    warmup_tokens: 1024
batching:
  emulate_prod_batch: true
  batch_sizes: [1,4,8]
```
Aisha: run command: `python tools/calibrate.py --config tools/calibrate.yaml --deploy false`
Ben: note for the experiment matrix: we should record kernel selection, per-layer scale histograms, and real runtime traces including KV cache hit/miss counts. currently our profiler exposes `kv_cache.hits` and `kernel_choice` logs.
Maria: I can add a small analysis script to compute kernel-switch regressions and attach a per-layer delta table. want that in CSV.
Carlos: volunteer to run on gpus in eng-cluster A tomorrow morning. I'll run three arms: per-tensor baseline, per-channel full, and two-pass hybrid.
calib-bot: scheduled job 1769460001 on cluster=eng-cluster-A image=calib-runner:v2. Logs will stream to /runs/1769460001/
Aisha: thanks — after Carlos run, we'll compare throughput, p99 latency, and eval loss on the eval prompt set. if two-pass gives <1% quality delta vs full per-channel but saves >5% throughput, ship two-pass as default. :thumbsup:
Ben: one more thought — we should record kernel microbenchmarks separately (no KV) to separate quant effects from caching effects.
Maria: added to checklist.
Carlos: ok i'll post results in this thread tomorrow. anyone want to pair on interpreting kernel histograms?
Aisha: Ben + Maria please. i'll own rollout decision.
Ben: lgtm :eyes:
Maria: thanks, pairing on histograms tomorrow. :+1:
